construct: PLP1 variants disrupt proteolipid protein 1/DM20 production, folding, trafficking, or availability in oligodendrocyte membranes. Because these proteins are major components of central nervous system myelin, the result is hypomyelination and progressive neurologic dysfunction, usually in males with X-linked inheritance.

distractor_audit.rationale: Alexander disease is a GFAP-related leukodystrophy characterized by abnormal astroglial Rosenthal fibers rather than the classic X-linked PLP1 hypomyelination pattern.
Krabbe disease is caused by GALC deficiency with toxic galactolipid accumulation and demyelination, not PLP1-related hypomyelination.
Canavan disease results from aspartoacylase deficiency and N-acetylaspartate accumulation rather than an X-linked myelin structural-protein defect.
Metachromatic leukodystrophy is a lysosomal sulfatide-storage disorder rather than the PLP1-associated X-linked hypomyelinating leukodystrophy.

educational_objective_text: Recognize Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease from early nystagmus, motor delay, diffuse hypomyelination, and an X-linked family pattern.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A male infant with nystagmus, hypotonia, delayed motor development, diffuse CNS hypomyelination, and a similarly affected maternal uncle strongly indicates X-linked PLP1-related Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Krabbe, Canavan, metachromatic leukodystrophy, and Alexander disease can all involve white matter, but their molecular defects and usual patterns do not explain the specific combination of early nystagmus, diffuse hypomyelination, male predominance, and maternal-line recurrence.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The imaging phenotype plus X-linked pedigree closes the main leukodystrophy alternatives and makes Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease uniquely best.
